subtitle: You Don't Make Cold, You Move Heat
teaser: Two hundred years from pond ice shipped to the tropics to a treaty every country on earth signed.

curve.label: U.S. households with a mechanical refrigerator
sources: 1940 Census of Housing (44% mechanical) — see research/chapter-04-cold-comes-home.md

quotes.text: You don't make cold. There's no such thing. You move heat.
quotes.speaker: Jeff Keltner
quotes.context: on why the coils on the back of your fridge are warm

quotes.text: The technology that wins isn't always the one that works. It's the one with the existing capital on its side.
quotes.speaker: Cyrus Mistry
quotes.context: on why John Gorrie's working ice machine lost to frozen pond water for forty years

quotes.text: Four fluids. And every single one of them was the safe one, the day it was chosen.
quotes.speaker: Jeff Keltner

quotes.text: The South got the future first because it got cut off from the past.
quotes.speaker: Cyrus Mistry
quotes.context: on how a Civil War blockade made New Orleans the first American city to run on machine-made ice

quotes.text: Efficiency is a scenario. Demand is a fact.
quotes.speaker: Cyrus Mistry
quotes.context: on what comes next for cooling

quotes.text: For anything that's spreading fast, the question isn't 'what's wrong with it today.' It's 'what's harmless at a thousand and dangerous at a billion?'
quotes.speaker: Jeff Keltner
quotes.context: on the monitoring program that caught the ozone hole

stats.label: of U.S. homes had a mechanical refrigerator, 1930 to 1950
stats.context: The steepest stretch of the curve ran straight through the Great Depression.

stats.label: of American homes had no refrigeration at all in 1940. No icebox, no fridge.
stats.context: In the South, six in ten nonwhite households had none.

stats.label: refrigerators were running on Freon by 1935, five years after GM and DuPont started making it.
stats.context: The safe gas that made the kitchen fridge possible, and later punched a hole in the sky.

stats.context: The curve America finished by 1950 is still near the bottom for hundreds of millions of people.

compare.title: Faster than the phone. Slower than TV.
